To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a single nucleotide deletion in the p52 gene coding sequence, leading premature signal termination of p53 protein translation, generates a p53 gene null allele by preventing the transport of mutant mRNA into the cytoplism.

a single base deletion in the p54 gene coding region, leading to premature termination of translation of the p54 gene, generates a null-allele by preventing transport of the mutant allele mRNas into the cytoplism.

a single base deletion in the p54 gene, which is the most common mutation in Li-Fraumenie patients, generates a null p53 allele by preventing transport into the cytoplams of mutant allele mRNNs, thus leading to unizygosity of the p53 gene in the germline and predisposition to multiple tumors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of p53 mutations in Li-Fraumenl Syndrome (LFS).
understanding the genetic mechanisms underlying the Li-Fraumemi syndrome.
understanding the molecular basis of cancer predisposition in the Li-Fraumani syndrome, and with identifying the genetic events that lead to cancer in these families.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the LFS phenotype is the result of the unizygote status of the p53 locus in the germ cells, and that this status is due to the loss of the p53 wild-type allele.
the Li-Fraumenti syndrome is a genetic disease caused by germline p53 gene mutations which result in the loss of the function of the wild-type allele.
p53 is a major tumor suppressor gene and that the loss of a wild-type p53 function is a necessary condition for the development of cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the p53 protein is not only a tumor suppressor but also a tumor initiator.
the Li-Fraumensy syndrome is due to the absence of the normal p53 allele in a cell.
we have shown that a single base change in p53 gene is sufficient to lead to LFS.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the p53 mutation may be present in a germ-line allele but may not be translated.
the loss of the p53 wild-type allele is the rate limiting step for tumor development in Li-Fraumenii syndrome.
the loss of the normal p53 allele is a sufficient event for tumor formation and that the loss of a single allele of p53 is sufficient to predispose to multiple cancers.
